title: Emergency funding can protect a rule without preserving the learning system
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office review of Department of Education Maintenance of Equity oversight during COVID-19 relief grant implementation
geography: United States; Department of Education, selected states and school districts

observations.period: 2021-2023; COVID-19 relief grant Maintenance of Equity implementation

denominator.unit: federal oversight and technical-assistance process reviewed by GAO

equity_rule.value: generally prohibited disproportionate cuts to districts or schools serving high percentages of low-income students

written_ta_procedures.value: not developed for MOEquity technical assistance
written_ta_procedures.unit: Department of Education internal procedure status

data_reliability.value: unreliable or incomplete data limited identification of poorest districts and assessment of intended results

lesson_sharing.value: not ensured by a documented procedure and not prioritized during implementation

observations.method: GAO review of federal laws, Education guidance and data, selected-state implementation, and interviews with Education officials and officials from seven states; detailed school-level analysis used six states with reliable data.
observations.uncertainty: Selected-state implementation and documentation gaps do not estimate national compliance, funding misallocation, or student-outcome effects.
observations.subgroup: States, districts, and schools subject to MOEquity requirements, with emphasis on high-poverty schools and districts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Education reported that some other programs maintain internal question-and-answer banks and data-governance structures; the finding is specific to MOEquity implementation and its documented procedures.

denominator.unit: states with reliable data used for GAO school-level analysis

poorest_school_identification.value: districts generally identified their poorest schools

poorest_district_identification.value: Education lacked reliable data to determine how states identified their poorest districts

intended_result.unit: whether MOEquity achieved its intended protection

observations.method: GAO analysis of Education data and selected state and district implementation records.
observations.uncertainty: The review does not show whether a particular school lost funding, whether supplemental payments were adequate, or what students experienced.
observations.subgroup: Selected states, districts, and schools; high-poverty status and supplemental funding are administrative categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: The data gap can coexist with real protection in many districts; inability to verify the intended result is not proof that the rule failed.

boundary: This record measures MOEquity oversight, data reliability, technical assistance, and institutional-learning gaps in a selected COVID-19 grant implementation. It does not estimate national compliance, funding loss, student outcomes, or future-crisis performance.
